name: Eye of Shadow
tactics: With a body made of little more than darkness and hate, an eye of shadow delights in its victims’ terror. It lurks in the darkness, waiting as its foes’ panic increases; then it strikes swiftly and viciously.

alignment.name: Evil
alignment.description:
Evil creatures don’t necessarily go out of their way to hurt people, but they’re perfectly willing to take advantage of the weakness of others to acquire what they want.
	Evil creatures use rules and order to maximize personal gain. They don’t care whether laws hurt other people. They support institutional structures that give them power, even if that power comes at the expense of others’ freedom. Slavery and rigid caste structures are not only acceptable but desirable to evil creatures, as long as they are in a position to benefit from them.

description: Creatures larger than Medium take up more than 1 square. For instance, an ogre takes up a space that is 2 squares by 2 squares. Most Large and larger creatures also have a reach greater than 1, which means they can make melee attacks against creatures that aren’t adjacent to them. A creature’s basic body shape usually determines its reach; a Large ogre has a reach of 2, but a Large horse has a reach of 1.

traits.name: All-Around Vision
traits.details: Enemies can’t gain combat advantage by flanking the eye of shadow.

traits.name: Combat Advantage
traits.details: The eye of shadow deals 2d6 extra damage to any creature granting combat advantage to it.

traits.name: Shadow Surge
traits.details: The eye of shadow regains 20 hit points at the end of its turn if it has remained invisible since the start of its turn.

effect.description: The beholder uses one or two of the following eye rays without provoking an opportunity attack. Each eye ray must target a different enemy.

hit.description: radiant damage, and the target is blinded until the end of its next turn.
thunder damage, and the target is deafened until the end of its next turn.
necrotic damage, and the target is immobilized (save ends). Until the effect ends, the beholder and shadow creatures have concealment while within 5 squares of the target.

effect.description: The beholder teleports 20 squares and becomes invisible until it attacks or until the end of its next turn.

hit.description: The target grants combat advantage until the end of the beholder’s next turn.
